F21 Relationship to host platform

Host platform

◐ partial

F01 Loop and built-in tools

Loop shape

F01.loop-shape How a turn runs: plan, tool call, result, stop.

● supported

Value: A turn of the agent loop runs from receiving a prompt to producing a response. In the SDKs, read-only tools (like Read, Glob, Grep, and MCP tools marked as read-only) can run concurrently; tools that modify state (like Edit, Write, Bash) run sequentially. query() creates the agentic loop and returns an async iterator used to stream messages.

Evidence:

  • E-claude-code-00426

    * **`claude_code.interaction`:** wraps a single turn of the agent loop, from receiving a prompt to producing a response.

    Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • E-claude-code-00172

    calls in a single turn, both SDKs can run them concurrently or sequentially depending on the tool. Read-only tools (like `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, and MCP tools marked as read-only) can run concurrently. Tools that modify state (like `Edit`, `Write`, and `Bash`) run sequentially to avoid conflicts.

    Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • 1 more on the sources page

Turn and step limits

F01.turn-limits Caps on turns, steps or tokens per run, and stop conditions.

◐ partial

Value: max_turns (Python) and maxTurns (TypeScript) cap agentic turns (tool-use round trips); a session that reaches its turn limit ends with a result message of subtype error_max_turns. The CLI flag --max-turns limits agentic turns and exits with an error when the limit is reached.

Limitation: The --max-turns CLI flag is "print mode only" and has "No limit by default"; "A session does not time out on its own" (no top-level session timeout).

Evidence:

Automatic compaction

F02.auto-compaction When and how history is summarized without a command.

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: Claude Code automatically compacts conversation history when you approach context limits, which preserves important code and decisions while freeing space. In the SDK, it summarizes older history, keeping recent exchanges and key decisions, and emits a system message with subtype compact_boundary. A PreCompact hook fires on a compaction request.

Persistent memory

F02.persistent-memory Memory that survives sessions: files, notes or an auto-memory store.

● supported

Value: Claude can persist learnings across sessions using auto memory: notes Claude writes for itself based on your corrections and preferences, stored per git repository under ~/.claude/projects/. The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the MEMORY.md index loads at the start of every session. /memory can enable or disable auto memory. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 disables it.

Output and blocking semantics

F06.output-blocking Exit codes or JSON that allow, deny, ask or modify.

◐ partial

Value: A `PreToolUse` hook runs before the rest of the permission flow and can allow, deny, or modify requests; if it rejects a tool call, the call doesn't execute and Claude receives the rejection message. A `TeammateIdle` hook exits with code 2 to send feedback and keep the teammate working.

Limitation: A hook that returns `allow` does not skip the deny and ask rules; a `PreToolUse` hook allow also can't approve an `rm` or `rmdir` removal targeting a critical path.

Matcher semantics

F06.matchers How a hook selects the tool or event it fires on.

● supported

Value: The `matcher` field matches a different value depending on the hook event: tool-based hooks match the tool name, while `Notification` hooks match the notification type. Use a single string with `|` to match multiple tools (for example `Edit|Write`); a JSON array means the hook never fires. An empty `matcher` on a Notification hook fires on all notification types.
